answer: A nebula of cheap fake identities collapses when influence requires passing randomized, independent audits rather than merely existing. Each agent's actions leave a quartz-clear behavioral fingerprint, and unrelated auditors compare patterns across accounts; clusters sharing timing, phrasing, and transaction trails are quarantined at their nadir of trust. Because one operator cannot convincingly diversify thousands of histories at once, forging a crowd costs more than the influence it buys.
